title: Violin
summary: Not yet indistinguishable from a real violin. Pressure comes from a compact receiver and the body's modes stop at 5 kHz. E5 is too dark, A4 sounds cleaner than the recording, B6 does not hold a steady note, and the stopped notes score below the open ones. Four Dominant strings (Pickering's sections), each with two polarisations, drive a computed shell of the Guarneri il Cannone's scanned geometry in spruce and maple, with its enclosed air through an f-hole neck. The bow grips through the friction law measured on real rosin, except on B3, which keeps a Stribeck curve. G3, D4, A4 and E5 use a bow of finite width with hair compliance. G3 also carries the air load on the shell's outside (the skin). Stopped notes press a fingertip on the string with 3.5 N and carry no finite-width bow; of them only B5 carries the strings' residual flexibility. The open strings are tuned to equal temperament, never to a recording.
physics_present: four strings from compiled Dominant section packs (Pickering 1985), each with two transverse polarisations; all four stay coupled through the bridge while one is bowed

a computed shell body from il Cannone's scanned geometry (Guarneri 1743) with the corrected f-hole shape: Norway spruce (Viala 2020) for the top, bass bar and soundpost, sycamore maple (Sonderegger 2013) for the back, ribs and bridge, 134 modes on the 6 mm mesh
the enclosed air as one cavity through a physical f-hole neck, its conductance from a boundary-element computation of the f-holes

on G3, at 192 kHz: the air load on the shell's outside from a boundary-element computation (the body-radiation skin), with the f-hole neck's outer end handed to it. It changes how the body moves, not how the note is picked up. With it alone the air mode's Q is 52, against 19 printed (Jansson) and 19 without it. Nothing is dropped: the skin radiates into full space, which is right for a body this small against the wavelength, where the older compact neck end radiated into a half-space and so matched the print for the wrong reason. The viscous loss at the edge of each measured f-hole is now added on G3, each hole the circle of its own area with its own wall thickness (5.31 cm2 and 2.51 mm, 4.98 cm2 and 2.28 mm) and the air flow split between them by conductance: it takes the air mode's Q to 30 at 275.6 Hz, where the row was predicted to put it, and the rest of the gap to the printed 19 is unexplained. No control ran on that render's binary
the steady-sliding friction law measured on real rosin (Woodhouse and Galluzzo 2025, eq. 13) on every note except B3
a bow of finite width (10 mm in 3 cells) with hair compliance after Pitteroff and Woodhouse 1998, on G3, D4, A4 and E5
the exact static compliance of each string's omitted modes at its bridge (residual flexibility), on the open notes G3, D4, A4 and E5, and on the stopped B5
a rigid fingertip pressed onto the string with 3.5 N (Issanchou et al. 2017 contact law), held by a static preload, on the stopped notes B3, B4, B5 and B6
longitudinal string waves and thermochemical room air (N2, O2, Ar, CO2) on A4; dry air (N2 0.8, O2 0.2) as one gas state on the other notes
open strings tuned to equal temperament (A4 = 440 Hz) by a tension factor read from the assembled instrument's own pulse response, never from a recording
physics_missing: a radiating exterior: pressure on every page is the shell's volume and the cavity at 1 m through a compact receiver, with no directivity and no finite receiver

enough sound for the plates' motion: between about 1250 and 2000 Hz the plates move about as much per newton as Bissinger's print, within 4 dB, but give 3 to 8 dB too little sound on a finite receiver and 10 to 13 dB on the compact receiver the pages use; his two sets reach the critical line at about 3.5 and 4.3 kHz, and ours doesn't by 4 kHz
body modes above 5 kHz, and any mesh convergence: every page is on the 6 mm mesh's 134 modes
air modes beyond the one cavity
the strings' tension loss: no printed loss exists for these strings
the string-to-bridge joint's contact mechanics: an authored spring and dashpot per string (200000 N/m, 0.1 N s/m)

residual flexibility on the stopped notes B3, B4 and B6 (B5 carries it since the row accepts the finger's preload): their cards were made when the static preload refused the row, "released static preload does not include the obstacles' residual compliance", so those cards drop it
the finite-width bow and hair compliance on the stopped notes
the measured rosin law on B3, which keeps a Stribeck curve (0.8 static, 0.4 kinetic, 0.1 m/s)
friction beyond steady sliding: no rosin temperature and no friction memory
string modes above about 9.6 kHz on the E string, which carries 17 sines, so B6's 5th harmonic has no string mode under it
a player: constant bow speed and force, where the real E5 keeps swelling for about a second after it speaks
one co-characterised instrument: il Cannone's geometry is combined with independently sourced wood and string data
